articles.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack, Source Code Reportedly Compromised
articles.summary:
Enterprise software giant SAP has confirmed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident following reports that threat actors targeted its development infrastructure.
German publication Der Spiegel [paywalled] broke the news on Thursday, citing SAP insiders and an internal notification sent to employees.
SAP told SecurityWeek that it had detected suspicious activity and implemented measures to protect customers and secure its services. The German company did not disclose details of the attack.
“Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data,” SAP told SecurityWeek.
German news agency DPA reviewed internal SAP communications that revealed the suspicious activity had been identified within GitHub.
According to an insider cited by Der Spiegel, the hackers obtained SAP employees’ authentication tokens, enabling them to copy and alter source code stored on GitHub.
SAP publishes developer tools, sample applications, and open source projects on GitHub. It’s unclear whether the threat actor accessed any proprietary code.
Separately, Handelsblatt reported that SAP’s emergency security measures have affected numerous teams. The software giant has reportedly replaced signing keys, limited access to GitHub, and suspended automated development operations.
None of the reports indicate that tampered code was incorporated into software delivered to SAP customers.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Series SSD with Over 18 Million Random Read IOPS
articles.summary:
Kioxia is introducing the GP2 Series SSD, and the standout number is more than 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size. I think we actually saw a precursor to this drive a few weeks ago. 18M IOPS is nearly double the performance of the GP1 Series Kioxia showed in August at FMS. The new drive is designed for PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3, and Kioxia says it is also expecting sequential read throughput of up to 28GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Kioxia GP2 Series Launched
The GP series is designed for a specific role in AI systems. Instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM to a GPU system, operators can use these NAND-based drives to create a flash-based memory tier the GPU can access directly. This lets the system handle larger datasets at a lower cost. Whenever you try to replace DRAM with NAND, endurance becomes a question. At 50DWPD, the GP2 is a step above many of the common capacity-focused drives.

Dans les remerciements, il explique avoir développé une partie de ses démonstrations en discutant pendant des mois avec GPT-6 Astra, le modèle d’OpenAI.

articles.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
articles.summary:
Hex, the package manager for Elixir and Erlang, fell victim to a cyberattack involving unauthorized access to its web servers.
The incident occurred on November 23, when the attackers exploited a vulnerability in hex.pm to execute commands. The attack was immediately blocked, and the underlying security defect was addressed within 20 minutes.
Between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC, the attacker sent 69 malicious requests, affecting six web servers. At 18:30, Hex replaced all hex.pm servers with patched versions rejecting the payload, and its firewall rule fully blocked the attacker’s traffic at 18:33.
“We found no evidence of unauthorized package modifications, database changes, or that the attacker maintained access to our systems,” the package manager explains.
According to Hex, potential access to database contents, such as email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes, sessions, second factor authentication secrets, and audit logs, cannot be ruled out.
While all the observed reads of private packages came from Hex servers, any read from a compromised server would appear legitimate, it says. Additionally, database and private documentation reads are not logged, hindering visibility into potential data exposure.
“The attacker’s commands could read the credentials our servers use, so we replaced them: the storage, CDN, email and database credentials, and the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. This logged everyone out of hex.pm and Hex clients,” Hex notes.

articles.title: 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach
articles.summary:
The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) has disclosed a data breach impacting data that residents uploaded to the myColorado application.
Colorado’s official mobile application, myColorado is used for digital identification, state services, and document storage. It has approximately 2.1 million users.
OIT took the application offline last week, after identifying unauthorized access to platform data, and immediately initiated incident response and an investigation into the incident.
One week after the outage began, OIT said it discovered the incident after the attackers triggered the automated threat detection systems deployed within its Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment.
The investigation has determined that the attackers accessed documents stored within the ‘myCards and Documents’ section of the application, which includes user-uploaded data, such as PDF files and photos of government IDs, vehicle registrations, and insurance cards.
According to Colorado, approximately 100,000 individuals might have been affected, but no payment information was accessed.
“Staff are working around the clock to match the inappropriately accessed documents to individual users. As that matching continues, OIT will further refine estimates on the number of people whose data was involved,” Colorado said.
The myColorado application remains offline and OIT has not announced a restoration date. The state expects to start sending direct notifications to the affected individu…

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

Versiones que no coinciden

SWE-2.1 doubles its predecessor’s Terminal-Bench score

articles.summary:
Wenn KI den schnellen Content liefert: Wie sich Marketingteams neu aufstellen müssen
Der breitflächige Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz bei der Content-Erstellung sorgt für eine enorme Masse an Inhalten, deren Produktionskosten verschwindend gering sind. Das wirkt sich nicht zuletzt auch auf Marketingabteilungen aus. Sie stehen vor der Frage: Wie muss eine Neuorganisation aussehen, wenn ihr Kern-Asset kaum noch etwas kostet?
Die Knappheit verschiebt sich zum menschlichen Urteilsvermögen
Durch KI ist Content nun Massenware. Binnen weniger Minuten ist ein Text erstellt. Die Hürde, vor einem leeren Blatt zu sitzen und den ersten Gedanken zu formulieren, fällt weg. Allerdings hat der KI-Einsatz einen erheblichen Nachteil: Die Ergebnisse sind Texte mit einer frappierenden Gleichförmigkeit und auffällig gut strukturierten Textbausteinen. Diese zunehmende Ähnlichkeit des Outputs haben Forscher University of Exeter und des University College London in einer Studie anhand von Kurzgeschichten gezeigt.
Hier entstehen zwei Dynamiken, die Beachtung verdienen. Die eine ist ein mögliches Qualitätsproblem. Eine KI wählt aus der Menge an Textbausteinen und Informationen die wahrscheinlichste Zusammensetzung eines Inhaltes und nicht zwangsläufig die richtige. Sie arbeitet mit Statistik, ihr fehlen Edge-Cases und Outlier, weshalb sich jeder Inhalt irgendwann liest, wie der des Nachbarn.
Die andere Entwicklung ist ökonomischer Natur, denn die Knappheit wandert vom Inhalt zur kritischen Urteil…

articles.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
articles.summary:
A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.
Found by ANSSI's Jérémy Jean (who submitted a fix in August), the flaw has been dubbed NFS2ROOT by cybersecurity firm OpenSec, which shared a full remote-root exploit and a patch with the NFSD maintainers in late September.
The vulnerability has existed since Linux kernel version 3.16 (released in March 2014), and it stems from a heap buffer overflow weakness in the Linux NFS server (nfsd).
NFS2ROOT affects systems with a Linux kernel older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4-rc1 if nfsd (v4.1 or 4.2) is loaded and running and TCP port 2049 is reachable over the Internet.
Successful exploitation lets remote threat actors without privileges corrupt kernel memory and gain root access to vulnerable Linux servers exposed online through low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction.
In NFS2ROOT attacks, the threat actors can exploit this flaw by sending maliciously crafted requests that cause the NFS server to write data beyond an allocated memory buffer. This lets them read kernel memory, bypass KASLR (which protects kernel memory addresses), and place a callback that can execute a command in a released memory area.
When the attacker closes the NFS connection, the kernel executes the embedded command with root privileges, allowing the attacker to gain root control of the unpatched Linux server.

Navegar, abrir várias abas e alternar entre programas exigem mais da máquina do que há alguns anos.

“Quando um PC mais antigo ainda conta com um processador capaz e memória suficiente, atualizar seu armazenamento para um SSD pode ser uma maneira prática de melhorar sua capacidade de resposta e acompanhar essas demandas”, explica van Dinteren.

Welcher STREAM-Speicher passt zur Anlage?
Auf dem Papier sind beide Modelle nahezu identisch, beide haben eine Nennkapazität von 5,024 kWh. Der entscheidende Unterschied liegt darin, auf welchem Weg der Solarstrom in den Akku gelangt. Davon hängt ab, für wen sich welches Modell eignet.

Ein eingebauter Solarladeregler bestimmt, mit welcher Spannung und welchem Strom der Akku geladen wird, und ein integrierter Wechselrichter wandelt den Gleichstrom für das Hausnetz um. articles.title: Tirar una tostada un poco quemada por miedo al cáncer es un gesto muy común. La evidencia dice que puedes dejar de hacerlo
articles.summary:
Hay muchos mensajes en torno a la alimentación que hemos ido escuchando a lo largo de los años, como por ejemplo que comer algo que está un poco quemado puede provocar cáncer. Esto ha hecho que, por ejemplo, cuando tomamos una tostada y se quema un poco más de la cuenta, decidamos tirarla para empezar de cero o raspar sobre el fregadero para minimizar ese "riesgo". Pero... ¿Es verdad?
Podemos estar tranquilos. La respuesta corta a esta pregunta es "no", puesto que no hay pruebas sólidas de que comer pan o alimentos en general que estén un poco quemados aumente el riesgo de provocar cáncer en seres humanos.
¿De dónde viene? Este mensaje nos llega a raíz de experimentos que se hicieron con animales a los que se les expuso a alimentos muy quemados durante mucho tiempo. Pero cuando los epidemiólogos buscan este mismo efecto cancerígeno en una muestra humana muy amplia, el rastro prácticamente desaparece. Lo que sí es cierto es que los organismos europeos siguen recomendando no pasarse con el tostado por un principio básico de precaución.
Lo que hay detrás. La protagonista de esta historia se llama acrilamida, un compuesto químico que se forma de manera natural cuando alimentos ricos en almidón, como el pan, las patatas o las galletas, se cocinan a altas temperaturas al freírlos, hornearlos o tostarlos.

Ferreiro explica que las experiencias de nuestros padres y abuelos pueden convertirse en referencias importantes, incluso cuando no las hemos vivido personalmente. Por qué recordamos momentos aparentemente insignificantes

After cloud computing comes space computing, obviously, right? There’s a neat irony here: Real-world clouds can interfere with optical satellite links. In other words, cloud services on the ground can be held back by the weather they are named after.
Networking conglomerate NTT wants to enable a new era of communications above the clouds (literally) with a combined set of space computing and lunar infrastructure developments that draw heavily on its work in photonics and light-based computing.

articles.title: Fake Roblox cheats are delivering password-stealing malware to family computers

A Cybernews analysis of search data found more than 22 million cheat-related Roblox searches between 2018 and 2026, which gives attackers a very large pool of potential victims. Bitdefender and SOC Prime have each documented campaigns this year in which the counterfeit tools did their advertised job while quietly stealing data.
Cybernews measured demand by tracking how often people searched for cheat-related terms on Google and Yandex. It covered 17 games in 184 countries, using the most popular phrases in English and in local languages. Roblox accounted for over half of all the cheat searches. Adjusted for audience size, the platform drew 482 cheat searches per 1,000 players, ahead of Valorant at 434 and Call of Duty: Warzone at 408. Minecraft came in at 74.
The appeal of a free shortcut is easy to see. Roblox costs nothing to download, but experiences inside it can put top weapons, VIP perks and rare items behind paywalls of roughly $5 to $50.
Roblox reported average spending of $12.29 per player in the third quarter of 2026, when it counted 138 million daily active users. Children without access to a credit card look to YouTube and Google for scripts that automate the grinding, and that is where the trouble starts.

From there, the hacker could access customer names and email addresses, as well as non-secret internal metadata about the account. The company says it’s since disabled the affected GitHub account, added tighter controls and detection tools, and brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate its efforts. Dans l’Union justement, le DMA impose depuis mars 2024 d’accepter les moteurs concurrents, et le bilan tient en un chiffre : zéro lancement. Le 24 novembre, l’équipe Chrome de Google a publiquement rejoint le constat de Mozilla, décrivant un choix qui existe « sur le papier, pas dans les faits ».
Une ouverture verrouillée par les conditions d’Apple

Así lo recoge el artículo 17.3 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, al que puedes apelar si alguien las pone sin ese respaldo.
Qué dice el artículo 17.3. Este apartado de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal incluye la vigilancia entre los servicios comunes de interés general y lo dice de esta manera: “El establecimiento o supresión de los servicios de portería, conserjería, vigilancia u otros servicios comunes de interés general, supongan o no modificación del título constitutivo o de los estatutos, requerirán el voto favorable de las tres quintas partes del total de los propietarios que, a su vez, representen las tres quintas partes de las cuotas de participación”.
Dos mayorías a la vez. Esto significa que la instalación tiene que aprobarse en la junta de propietarios y que el recuento se hace dos veces, por número de propietarios y por cuotas de participación. Vamos, que no basta con reunir a tres de cada cinco propietarios si entre todos no suman también tres quintas partes de las cuotas. Eso sí, esa mayoría es el primer requisito, pero no el único.
Hacia dónde pueden apuntar. Pero aunque la junta dé su aprobación, las cámaras no pueden grabar cualquier cosa. La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) aclara en sus preguntas frecuentes sobre comunidades que “no podrán ca…

AWS Nitro Sandboxes give AI agents a place to run
A coding agent has written a script and wants to run it. The script may do exactly what the developer asked. The next decision, though, belongs to humans.
The team building the system has to answer a slew of questions: Where should that code run? What should it be able to reach once it starts?
The script doesn’t get a vote.
At the recent KubeCon + CloudNativeCon conference in Salt Lake City, The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois asked AWS Senior Product Manager Mike Stefaniak what’s keeping more teams from running agents in production.
Stefaniak said he’s seen a handful of large customers commit in a big way. Many others are still figuring out security and identity. AWS Nitro Sandboxes, announced at the conference, address one part of that problem by giving developers an isolated place to run container workloads.
Keep the image, change where it runs
Stefaniak describes Nitro Sandboxes as a way to bring the isolation of the Nitro hypervisor to multiple workloads within one EC2 instance. Each sandbox draws CPU and memory from the parent instance.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
On EKS Auto Mode or ECS Managed Instances, Stefaniak says, a runtime configuration tells AWS to place the workload in a sandbox.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
That’s important to a developer with an existing build pipeline who wants to change how a workload runs without rebuilding the application around a new packaging mod…

articles.title: PCB Grounding Design and Return Path
articles.summary:
Many PCB design guidelines reduce grounding to a few rules:
- Separate analog and digital ground
- Connect power ground and signal ground at a single point
- Cut out copper under switching nodes
These rules are not wrong, but they are incomplete. They do not answer a fundamental question: where does the current return?
If a ground plane is split and a signal crosses the gap, its return current may be forced to detour. The result can be higher electromagnetic radiation, even though the original intention was noise isolation. This article follows one main principle: design “ground” as a return path.
Why Ground Moves
Every copper trace, via, and ground plane has impedance.
At DC, copper resistance causes a voltage drop. When current changes rapidly, parasitic inductance also produces a voltage.
If a sensitive measurement branch shares part of its return path with a high-current branch, the voltage drop across that shared copper appears in the measurement branch.
The “ground” may then move with the high-current load. This is common-impedance coupling.
As shown above, loads farther along a shared return copper path use more common copper segments and may see larger ground-potential shifts. In a real PCB, current distribution and impedance vary with frequency, copper shape, and via structure; a single DC resistance cannot represent the return path. articles.title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028
articles.summary:
Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system.
Introduced in 2005 as Software Update Services (SUS), WSUS (Windows Server Update Services) lets IT administrators manage and distribute updates for Microsoft products across corporate networks with many Windows devices.
It gives admins centralized control over the updates, rather than having each device download them individually from Microsoft's servers.
Microsoft has officially deprecated WSUS in September 2024, but said that it still plans to maintain functionality and continue publishing updates through the channel. The change affects enterprise environments that rely on WSUS to manage updates delivered to many devices but does not impact home users or those using Microsoft Configuration Manager.
In a recently updated support document, Microsoft went even further and confirmed that Windows Server 2028 removes the WSUS server role altogether.
"WSUS remains available and supported in earlier Windows Server releases, including Windows Server 2025, for the duration of each release's support lifecycle. You can continue to use WSUS on those releases to manage updates for supported Windows client and Windows Server releases, which includes updates to Windows Server 2028," it said.
"Microsoft recognizes the need to manage updates in disconnected and highly controlled environments. We're invested in supporting these scenarios and we'll share more as the work…

articles.title: La reflexión de Albert Einstein sobre las personas independientes: "La monotonía y la soledad de una vida tranquila estimulan la mente creativa"

En octubre de 1933, durante una intervención en Londres, el físico defendió que algunos empleos tranquilos podían ser una buena alternativa para quienes necesitaban tiempo libre para investigar. La frase, recuperada por OKDIARIO en un artículo sobre las personas independientes, resumía algo que Einstein valoraba especialmente: poder dedicar horas a pensar sin demasiadas interrupciones.

El científico consideraba que trabajar en un faro podía dejar tiempo suficiente para estudiar matemáticas o filosofía. La idea tenía su lógica: en lugar de depender de una beca de investigación, un joven podría tener un empleo con el que mantenerse y reservar parte del día para desarrollar sus propios proyectos.
Einstein también cuestionó las dificultades que encontraban quienes recibían ayudas para investigar. A su juicio, la obligación de presentar resultados en periodos demasiado cortos podía perjudicar trabajos que necesitaban años de dedicación. Por eso pensaba que disponer …

Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

As is always the case when machines enter the workplace, Volvo claims the idea is for the robots to take on some of the more repetitive and physically demanding jobs, but there's always the specter of replacement in instances like these.
Ghent is the first Volvo plant to try the AEON humanoids, built by Swedish technology group Hexagon. Volvo employees show the robots how to place components precisely into two fixtures, and the machines learn by copying them. Once they can do that reliably, the team will teach them to handle several parts, move around the production area, and work with the plant's automated equipment.
AEON stands about 5 feet 5 inches tall, weighs 132 pounds, and can carry 22 pounds. One decidedly unhuman feature is the set of wheels that can propel it across the factory floor at just over 5 mph. The appeal for Volvo is that AEON can move between workstations designed for people, something a robotic arm bolted to the floor would struggle to do, obviously.
More robots are due in Ghent for a larger pilot in the first half of 2027. Volvo wants them working on the production line by the middle of the year, though it hasn't said how many will join the workforce or what that might mean for the people currently doing those jobs.

Avi Davidson has volunteered to find out how a bionic hand that feels might alter his brain and nervous system.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist.
He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi's arm. He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with.
Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy) and writing (also not easy).
What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself.
He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. A diferencia de las aplicaciones piratas que requieren instalación en el teléfono, estos sitios operan directamente desde el navegador web, exponiendo tanto a computadoras como a dispositivos móviles a vectores de ataque diseñados para vulnerar la privacidad y el sistema operativo.
Malvertising y capas invisibles (Clickjacking)
Ni Futbol Libre ni Roja Directa alojan señales de televisión propias; su infraestructura consiste en indexar enlaces de terceros y monetizar el tráfico mediante redes de publicidad maliciosa (malvertising). Para maximizar los clics forzados, los reproductores de video integrados en estas páginas están cubiertos por capas transparentes (clickjacking).
Al intentar iniciar la transmisión del partido, quitar el silencio o ampliar la pantalla, el usuario es redirigido automáticamente a dominios externos. Estas páginas emergentes suelen simular alertas del sistema operativo que exigen descargar supuestos códecs de video, actualizaciones de reproductores o extensiones obligatorias para ver la final. articles.title: Researcher finds unprotected database with about 2 billion credentials, the largest he's ever seen
articles.summary:
Ripple effect: Ethical security researcher Jeremiah Fowler recently uncovered a massive unsecured database containing around two billion potentially compromised account credentials. A single database was apparently hosting several collections of account credentials from multiple security incidents, and anyone could download the data before the host decided to block access.
Fowler said that the database he discovered was neither protected by a password nor encrypted in any way. Around 2 billion credentials were just sitting there, waiting for someone to grab the data and use it to launch further attacks against users. The dataset included email addresses, logins and other user IDs, passwords, and more.
The researcher probed the online database by reviewing the neatly organized data, finding additional content types such as application credentials, browser passwords, cookies, session tokens, and other "identifiers." Fowler said that this was the largest collection of compromised accounts he had ever found. The dataset was more than 13 times bigger than an exposure he previously reported and included a lot more device-specific data for potential attackers to exploit.
The database was also noteworthy for how the plaintext data was organized in thousands of different folders, with some documents grouped by country-code top-level domain. Around 400,000 documents appeared to come from advanced malware threats, as they were stored in separate folders focused on individual victims.

En realidad, lo primero que recomienda es bastante sencillo: retirar la suciedad visible antes de desinfectar. Así lo explica también el artículo publicado por Clarín, que recoge sus consejos y las indicaciones de los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) de Estados Unidos.
El error de mezclar productos para limpiar el váter
Para empezar, utiliza un limpiador adecuado para el baño y frota las zonas donde haya suciedad. Después tendrás que aclarar los restos del producto siguiendo sus instrucciones. Si necesitas desinfectar, aplica un desinfectante compatible con la superficie y respeta el tiempo que indica el fabricante. No sirve de mucho retirarlo antes de que haya actuado.
Pero hay una advertencia especialmente importante: nunca mezcles lejía con vinagre, amoniaco ni otros limpiadores. Algunas combinaciones pueden desprender gases tóxicos, así que tampoco conviene echar lejía directamente en un inodoro donde todavía quedan restos de otro producto. Además, es recomendable mantener el baño ventilado mientras limpias.

Printing an advanced transistor and manufacturing a commercially viable chip are two very different achievements. The distinction deserves greater attention in Washington’s semiconductor export control debate.

While the immediate dispute centers on ASML and immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, the legislation raises a broader question: How much of China’s manufacturing capability depends on foreign equipment that measures and controls production rather than creates semiconductor structures?
As transistor architectures and advanced packaging become more complex, the answer increasingly lies in metrology and inspection.
The economics of yield
Gate-all-around (GAA) transistors require precise control of nanosheet dimensions, epitaxial layer thickness, and material composition. Small variations can affect threshold voltage, carrier mobility, and device performance. Advanced packaging introduces additional challenges, particularly in surface preparation, bonding alignment, and interconnect integrity.
Consider a simplified assembly containing eight known-good dies and requiring seven bonding operations. Assuming independent bonding outcomes, a 99% yield per operation produces a cumulative bonding yield of approximately 93%. At 97%, it falls to 81%, even before accounting for other manufacturing losses.

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

articles.title: Série noire aux États-Unis : des pirates se sont infiltrés dans Cloud One, la plateforme cloud géante de l’US Air Force
articles.summary:
L’intrusion dans le cloud de l’armée de l’air américaine a été repérée il y a environ un mois, au cours de travaux de mise à niveau du système, selon deux des sources de Reuters.
D’après une dépêche du 27 novembre de l’agence de presse Reuters, qui s’appuie sur cinq sources anonymes, des pirates ont réussi à pénétrer Cloud One, la plateforme cloud phare de l’US Air Force.
Lancée en 2017 avec Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle et Alphabet, elle fait tourner des dizaines d’applications, de la paie à la logistique, mais aussi des outils sensibles comme celui qui rassemble les données radar de défense aérienne de toute l’Amérique du Nord.
Les pirates ont atteint le cœur de la plateforme
Interrogée par Reuters, l’Air Force a seulement répondu qu’elle ne commentait pas « la posture de sécurité, les vulnérabilités ou l’état opérationnel » de ses réseaux. Les détails recueillis par l’agence de presse restent maigres. On ne sait ni qui sont les pirates, ni jusqu’où ils sont allés, ni si des données ont été volées.
D’après une des sources de Reuters, les attaquants ont exploité une vulnérabilité logicielle pour atteindre le « control plane », la couche d’administration du cloud, qu’elle compare à une télécommande universelle. Un tel accès permettrait en théorie de consulter l’état opérationnel des avions militaires ou de suivre les mouvements de pièces détachées, sans que l’on sache si les pirates l’ont fait.
Signe de la gravité de l’incident, le Cyber Command, le commandement militaire américa…

articles.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
articles.summary:
When discussing IT infrastructure security, the focus is usually on firewalls, EDR, backup, vulnerability management, and network segmentation. However, all of them are effective only under one condition — if the infrastructure itself is under control.
Incidents often begin not with the exploitation of a vulnerability or bypassing protection systems, but with shortcomings in basic infrastructure management. Every virtual machine, server, access, and IP address must have an owner, a lifetime, and a controlled path for creation and deletion.
When management processes are opaque, the infrastructure itself becomes a source of information security risks, and security tools have to operate over an unknown environment and merely contain the consequences.
This principle is equally critical for enterprise companies and service providers — regardless of whether the platform serves internal services, development teams, or external customers, a loss of control over administration can lead to the compromise of the entire environment.
Why Security Grows Out of Manageability
In modern IT infrastructure, hundreds of systems run on the same resources, and the environment itself is constantly changing — dozens of services are created, scaled, and deleted daily.

articles.title: A 1950s elevator just sent a message through a brick wall using nothing but gravity
articles.summary:
What just happened? These days, nearly every wireless signal around us, from those carrying Wi-Fi to 5G, can be stopped by a thick enough wall or a metal box. Gravity is different, since no known material can block or shield it. Physicists in Australia have now used that quirk to send a short message through a brick wall. Weirdly, the transmitter was just an old elevator in their own building.
The elevator in question sits inside the University of Queensland's Parnell Building and dates back to the 1950s. It has a 1.8-metric-ton counterweight that moves the opposite way whenever the car travels between floors, so the team treated one position of that weight as a 0 and the other as a 1. Then they ran the elevator up and down to spell out a binary message.
Meanwhile, the receiver was an off-the-shelf gravimeter sitting in a bathroom next to the shaft, behind a brick wall. Each time the weight moved, gravity at the sensor changed by just five billionths of its normal strength. Still, it was enough for the team to decode a single, rather fitting word: "Gravity."
The catch is that the old elevator needs about 25 seconds just to shift the counterweight. So the setup managed only one bit per minute.

This essay originally appeared in The Guardian. It’s an expanded version of the one I posted as “We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For.”
It’s been a bad week for our computerized infrastructure. We’ve seen outages at Microsoft, the FAA, a handful of banks, United Airlines, an unnamed classified NSA network, and Apple. People should be forgiven for suspecting a coordinated cyberattack, a common cause, or at least a conspiracy. But there is none.
The incidents are unrelated. They’re not the result of any cyberattack, coordinated or not. And, even more surprising, they don’t seem to be the result of AI. (We can’t say anything about the NSA; we’ll probably never know the details of that one.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.
None of them should surprise, though. Our computerized infrastructure is both vulnerable and fragile.
Much of it is old and has been incrementally patched and upgraded over the decades. A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense. There often aren’t good backup systems. And more and more of it is centralized, meaning that individual failures have cascading consequences across many different aspects of our lives and society.
A lot of our tech infrastructure just barely works. And when it fails, it can fail badly. It’s the very opposite of resilience.

articles.title: Allstate has been suffering an outage since Monday
articles.summary:
On Monday, November 23rd, Allstate began dealing with an outage that has impacted its website, mobile apps, and roadside assistance service. It’s just the latest company, including Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, to suffer an outage in the last few weeks. As of Friday afternoon, access to accounts through the app and site appeared to still be down. When asked for comment, the company pointed us to a notice on its site reading:
Allstate has been suffering an outage since Monday
One of the biggest insurance companies in the country has been dealing with a major outage for five days.
Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.
Opening the app pops up a notification saying the company is working to “restore access as soon as possible,” and encourages customers to contact the company by phone to file and manage claims. Users have flooded X and Reddit with complaints about the outage, some of whom have either been left waiting for roadside assistance or have been unable to insure new vehicles.
Allstate hasn’t publicly identified a cause for the outage.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Omata AI turns WhatsApp into a business operating system for SMEs
articles.summary:
Nigerian startup Omata AI has built a WhatsApp-native business operating system that helps small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) manage their day-to-day operations through simple conversations.
The flagship product of Autonomous Data Enterprise, a company founded in 2026 by Stanley Okafor, Omata AI lets merchants record sales, manage inventory, track customer balances and monitor business performance by sending WhatsApp messages. A connected dashboard gives them more oversight.
“Our vision is to make business management as easy as sending a WhatsApp message,” Okafor told Disrupt Africa. “For example, a trader can send a message such as, “I sold two bags of rice for NGN50,000”, and Omata AI can interpret the information, prepare a structured transaction and request the merchant’s approval before confirmation.”
Okafor said that many small businesses across Africa still rely on notebooks, memory and scattered WhatsApp chats to manage their records. Existing accounting, POS and inventory tools are often too complex or too costly for them.
“Rather than asking merchants to adapt to complicated software, we want business software to adapt to the way they already operate,” he said.
The startup’s main differentiator is what Okafor calls a “human-approval-first” architecture. Under this design, AI cannot change financial records without the business owner’s sign-off.

articles.title: Hunger strike outside Anthropic HQ enters third day as activist demands "AI might kill everyone" warning
articles.summary:
Sounding off: A lot of people are worried about the development of RSI, or recursive self-improvement, and their concerns are understandable. It's the concept of an AI system improving its own capabilities, with each improved version becoming better at making further improvements. One activist is so against RSI that he's holding a hunger strike outside Anthropic's San Francisco HQ. In an update on his third day there, he said he could go without food for 40 days or more.
Elliot Callender listed eight conditions and said he'd end his protest if any one of them were met. One that Anthropic could meet on its own is to put a warning on every one of its products under the heading "AI might kill everyone," which, in fairness, it warned could happen in its IPO prospectus.
Callender wants the company to explain why AI systems given very different goals might still find it useful to do things like acquire more resources or avoid being shut down. He also wants it to explain how long researchers have been discussing the risk of human extinction and point users to the infamous incident in which an OpenAI agent compromised accounts across four services, including Hugging Face.
Some of his other conditions are even less likely to happen. Callender says he would leave if Anthropic halted all AI research, development, and training and put at least 80% of its cash and revenue toward lobbying for a bilateral AI treaty. articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary:
AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  York University
- Summary:
  AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

articles.title: Mozilla Partners with Mistral to Bring Open-Weight AI Models to Firefox Smart Window
articles.summary:
Mozilla, the non-profit organisation behind the Firefox browser, has announced a partnership with Paris-based Mistral AI to bring the French company's open-weight models into Firefox Smart Window, Mozilla's AI browsing assistant currently in beta.
The deal introduces Mistral Small 4 as a recommended model for Smart Window users in France, the United States and Canada, with rollouts planned for the United Kingdom and Germany later this year. It coincides with Smart Window's first expansion beyond North America and marks a deliberate attempt by Mozilla to resist the pattern of browser makers coupling tightly to a single American AI provider.
Smart Window, originally announced in November 2025 as "AI Window", operates as an optional window separate from regular browsing. It helps users make sense of complex searches, group related tabs, revisit pages they have seen before and carry work across sessions. Users decide when to use it, which model to use and what browsing context to share. Conversations are not stored on Mozilla's servers by default, and Mistral has agreed to zero data retention for the partnership.
Mistral Small 4 is a 119-billion-parameter model distributed on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence. Mozilla selected it after evaluating performance in the beta, with multilingual quality as a central criterion. articles.title: Unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC gives remote code execution
articles.summary:
A zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform has been publicly disclosed, along with a proof-of-concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable servers.
The exploit, dubbed "4HTTP2SHELL" (previously 4HTTP2ROOT), was published on Thanksgiving Day by a cybersecurity researcher known as ek0ms savi0r from the Church of Malware, who demonstrated how the vulnerability can be exploited using just four HTTP requests.
Cacti is an open-source network monitoring and graphing tool used to monitor the performance of servers, routers, switches, firewalls, and other network infrastructure.
Because the software can store credentials and SNMP passphrases used to access or read data from monitored devices, compromising a Cacti server could potentially give attackers access to other systems on a corporate network.
The researcher published a technical write-up, a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, and a video demonstrating the attack in a GitHub repository named "Sad Girls 0day Club."
"I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests. No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface," explains the researcher.
The vulnerability stems from weak input validation that allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject SQL statements into the application's database and modify commands executed by Cacti's real-time poller.

articles.title: Victime d’une cyberattaque, l’AFP bloque une plateforme pour contrer les pirates
articles.summary:
L’Agence France-Presse (AFP) a été piratée dans la nuit du mercredi 25 au jeudi 26 novembre. Vers 1 h 30 du matin, « l’AFP a été la cible d’une cyberattaque » qui « visait AFP Forum, l’une des plateformes sur lesquelles nos clients consultent et téléchargent nos contenus », explique la direction. AFP Forum sert notamment aux rédactions pour acheter les photos et les vidéos qui illustrent leurs articles.
À lire aussi : La FIFA a été piratée – des données personnelles et professionnelles ont été compromises
« Temporairement inaccessible »
Dès que l’intrusion a été détectée, les équipes techniques ont « isolé la plateforme pour la protéger ». Par mesure de précaution, la plateforme est toujours « temporairement inaccessible » ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026. Cette mesure doit empêcher les pirates de faire plus de dégâts tant que la brèche n’a pas été colmatée. Aucune date de retour n’a été communiquée pour le moment.
Sans surprise, l’AFP a promptement ouvert une enquête. L’agence de presse indique que « des analyses sont en cours, avec l’appui d’experts extérieurs ». Pour le moment, l’AFP ne dispose « d’aucun élément sur l’identité des auteurs de cette attaque » contre l’une des trois grandes agences de presse mondiales.
Pour rappel, l’agence, qui emploie 1 840 journalistes et publie en moyenne 2 300 dépêches par jour, a déjà été piratée deux ans plus tôt. En septembre 2024, l’AFP a signalé une possible fuite de données à la CNIL, le gendarme français des données personnelles.

articles.title: Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
articles.summary:
Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
Hyderabad-based startup Hala Mobility provides electric vehicles to delivery riders, connects them with delivery companies, and offers early-salary financing and accident insurance.
Delivery riders can cover 100 to 120 km a day, often on petrol vehicles that aren’t designed for such intensive use. Rising fuel prices add to their operating costs.
Electric vehicles (EVs) can reduce these expenses, and delivery companies are encouraging riders to make the switch. However, riders who cannot afford or access an EV have little choice but to continue using petrol vehicles.
Access to a vehicle is only part of the problem. Riders also need to know how far it can travel on a charge, where to charge it, and where to get it serviced. For companies managing large EV fleets, the challenges extend to monitoring battery health, battery swaps, energy consumption, and maintenance schedules.
Hyderabad-based Hala Mobility aims to address these gaps through an EV fleet-as-a-service and multi-modal shared mobility platform that allows riders and delivery companies to use EVs without purchasing them.
Through the Hala app, riders can rent, lease or finance vehicles. Hala was founded in 2019 by Srikanth Reddy Kalakonda, Founder and CEO, and Co-founder Snehith Reddy Meda.

articles.title: Penguin Revives Retired DDR4 for AI Servers
articles.summary:
With DDR5 DRAM prices high and supply tight, Penguin Solutions is collaborating with Marvell to put DDR4 sitting in retired servers back to work.
Penguin’s eight-DIMM DDR4 Compute Express Link (CXL) add-in card uses Marvell’s Structera X controller to make qualified memory available as additional system capacity on compatible servers. The approach supplements server memory rather than requiring organizations to rely exclusively on DDR5 for expansion.
In a briefing with EE Times, Andy Mills, Penguin’s VP of advanced product development, said enterprises are looking to expand memory capacity while facing procurement and budget pressures. DDR4 recovered during server refreshes cannot go directly into DDR5 memory slots, he said, but Penguin’s approach can connect that older memory through a PCIe expansion card instead.
Penguin is launching the card as AI data centers take a growing share of DRAM. Mills said reusing DDR4 has been talked about for years, but the market shifted quickly, “once DDR5 prices went through the roof.”
The card targets applications that need more memory than a server’s DDR5 slots can accommodate, including EDA, graph workloads, and AI, Mills said. Penguin has also identified AI inference and in-memory databases as potential uses. The aim is to supplement server memory with reclaimed capacity rather than require customers to discard usable DDR4 during a platform transition.

articles.title: CAA members can get a $40/125GB Rogers plan for Black Friday
articles.summary:
Canadians on the hunt for a Black Friday wireless deal may want to check out Red Wireless’s promo.
Red Wireless is an authorized Rogers dealer and is currently offering CAA members two plans: $40/mo 125GB Canada/U.S. or $50/mo CAN/U.S./MEX with unlimited data.

Both of these plans are really solid offers, especially compared to what Rogers offers on its own website. The carrier currently has a $70/100GB plan and an $85 CAN/US/MEX plan with unlimited data, so you’re saving quite a bit with the Red Wireless offer.

Limited Demand Visibility and Growing Supply Chain Caution Heighten Risk of DRAM Contract Price Declines in 2028
TrendForce's latest memory industry findings indicate that supply chain participants have been reassessing their production and sales plans for 2027 and 2028 since early 4Q26, resulting in a slight slowdown in overall DRAM procurement momentum. 
This growing caution stems from concerns that the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections could affect the pace of future data center development, potential changes to NVIDIA's financing policies for neocloud providers, and geopolitical restrictions affecting the flow of advanced-node chips and access to leased computing resources.Given the uncertainty surrounding the extent to which these developments will affect demand, TrendForce has outlined two scenarios—a base case and a bear case—for DRAM contract price trends over the next two years. 
Under the base case, conventional DRAM contract price increases are expected to narrow progressively throughout 2027, with prices potentially leveling off in the second half of the year before declining in 2028.
The base case takes several demand-side factors into account. Consumer electronics manufacturers are facing mounting sales pressure and have limited capacity to absorb further price increases. articles.title: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Smartphone GPS, motion sensors, and vehicle interfaces can each report valid measurements that produce incorrect results when combined without accounting for timing and coordinate frames.
- Preserve raw observations and their provenance before synchronizing, transforming, or normalizing them.
- Introduce a quality gate that determines whether telemetry is suitable for a particular decision instead of forcing every observation into a definitive result.
- Design for real-world conditions, including delayed GPS updates, phone movement, background interruptions, and intermittent connectivity.
- Monitor data quality alongside conventional application and infrastructure metrics because a functioning pipeline can still produce unreliable driving events.
Why this matters: the phone is not the vehicle
A smartphone can provide a surprising amount of information about a journey, including GPS estimates location and speed, accelerometers measure motion along the device's axes, gyroscopes capture rotation, and others. A connected vehicle may expose additional signals, such as speed, engine state, or diagnostic information.
Combining these sources creates opportunities for fleet monitoring, usage-based insurance, driving-behavior analysis, trip reconstruction, and connected mobility services.
However, having more sensors does not automatically produce better telemetry.

articles.title: Character.AI wants to sell chat histories from more than 21 million accounts in bankruptcy, and 42 states object
articles.summary:
Editor's take: Private conversations that millions of people had with AI characters are up for auction, and 42 state attorneys general want the sale stopped. Character.AI, now in Chapter 11, is trying to sell the saved chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts, 2.1 million of them registered to minors, to a buyer who would owe those users nothing.
Character.AI built its product on persistent, role-playing conversations. Users talk with characters for weeks or months, and the company stores every exchange on its servers. That archive is now one of the few valuable things left in the bankrupt company, and the attorneys general say the plan offers "no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold."
The technical value of such a trove is easy to see. Long, emotionally candid dialogue is the kind of material used to train chatbots to sound more human and keep users engaged. The same material is also sensitive in a way ordinary web data is not. Chats with a companion bot can include confessions, relationship details, and discussions of self-harm. Linked to an account, they are hard to anonymize.
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October after years of scandals and lawsuits. These included legal challenges over teen suicides and a claim from Disney over characters that used its intellectual property. Disney later bought some of the company's assets and hired chief executive Karandeep Anand. A similarly broad coalition of attorneys general opposed that deal…

Several customers reported receiving the alerts despite having two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled on their accounts. However, when customers checked their accounts for connected devices, some found no unfamiliar devices listed.

articles.title: Huawei says it can build better memory chips than Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, but the proof is still to come
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Tech giant Huawei will reportedly present a white paper on its in-house HBM chip design that some industry insiders speculate could outperform existing products from market leaders Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The presentation will be made at the International Solid-State Circuits Conference in San Francisco on February 16, 2027.
Huawei's novel HBM design reportedly supports twice the data-pin density of the current products from the three leading players. According to Bloomberg, the new interface uses 4,096 data pins split across 64 channels - twice the width of the 2,048-bit interface of existing HBM products from Samsung and Hynix.
To pack twice as many connections into the same physical footprint, Huawei is reportedly using five-layer wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding to fuse memory controllers directly onto stacked DRAM dies. In theory, the new architecture could deliver higher memory bandwidth and better efficiency, allowing more data to be transferred to the processor at the same time while consuming less power.
If the theoretical improvements translate into real-world gains, Huawei's HBM chips could be better suited for model training, AI inference, data ingestion, and other complex tasks than competing products. However, five-layer wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding could be difficult to scale, especially without access to advanced lithography, so it remains to be seen how Huawei will overcome the challenge.

articles.title: Un trou de la couche d’ozone record et pourtant la situation n’est pas si grave : comment est-ce possible ?
articles.summary:
27,3 millions de kilomètres carrés. C’est la taille atteinte le 20 septembre 2026 par le trou de la couche d’ozone au-dessus de l’Antarctique, soit près de deux fois la superficie du continent glacé et 31 % de plus que la moyenne des vingt dernières années à la même période. Ces chiffres, communiqués par l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) le 26 novembre 2026, nous viennent du programme européen d’observation de la Terre Copernicus, et plus précisément de Sentinel-5P, un satellite chargé de surveiller l’état de l’atmosphère terrestre depuis 2017.
Ce trou est en réalité un appauvrissement de la couche d’ozone au-dessus de l’Antarctique, qui se forme chaque année au printemps austral, quand le froid extrême de la stratosphère polaire favorise la destruction de l’ozone. Le phénomène est saisonnier et dépend aussi du retour du soleil, mais il est d’abord provoqué par les activités humaines, et plus précisément par les CFC et autres gaz chlorés ou bromés longtemps utilisés dans les aérosols, les réfrigérateurs ou les climatiseurs. Voir l’un des plus grands trous en près d’un demi-siècle peut donc paraître inquiétant à première vue – pourtant, la situation n’est pas si simple, et surtout pas si catastrophique.

articles.title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
articles.summary:
Netflix has developed Quasar, an internal tool that identifies which repositories use specific library API symbols, helping engineering teams assess the downstream impact of proposed changes before releasing them. The tool combines semantic code indexing with API comparisons to identify affected consumers, dependency versions, and relevant call sites across repositories.
The challenge extends beyond identifying whether an API change is incompatible. Compatibility tools can flag a removed method or changed signature, but they do not necessarily identify which applications call it. Dependency graphs show declared relationships rather than actual usage, while text searches can miss references involving inheritance, overloads, and generated code. Building every downstream consumer to validate a change can also be expensive.
Quasar architecture diagram showing the indexing and query workflow (Source: Netflix Blog Post)
Quasar indexes symbol definitions and references using the SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol, an open format for representing code relationships. Language-specific indexers submit data during CI builds, which Quasar stores in Amazon S3 as Parquet files and queries through Amazon Athena.

À ce stade, personne ne prévoit de faire pareil, quand bien même le site est absolument stratégique pour lancer les fusées Ariane 6 et Vega-C.
Thierry Vallée, sous-directeur chargé de la protection, de la sauvegarde et de l’environnement au CSG, la base gérée par l’agence spatiale française, a été clair quand Numerama l’a interrogé sur place : « Pour le moment, on n’est pas du tout sur ce registre de neutralisation. » Le centre mise plutôt sur des brouilleurs et sur une très grande zone interdite de survol.
Ce choix s’explique d’abord par la géographie. Selon Thierry Vallée, le relatif isolement du Centre spatial guyanais (littéralement entre l’océan Atlantique et la jungle amazonienne) lui simplifie la tâche. La règlementation aussi : « La lutte anti-drone ici, elle est simplifiée par le fait qu’on est dans une zone qui naturellement est interdite de survol. »

Era el cénit de un periodo de cinco días que dejó esa zona del país unos 5 grados por debajo de lo habitual. Dos meses después, como suele hacer, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) repasó el invierno y llegó a la conclusión de que, con la información disponible, nada de lo que pasó en aquellos cinco días podía considerarse una ola de frío.
No dio la talla, no entró en la lista. Lo cual tampoco es raro, porque, en fin, la lista lleva sin tener nuevos miembros desde el 2 de marzo de 2023.
Eso quiere decir que llevamos tres inviernos completos sin una sola ola de frío. Nunca en toda la serie habíamos encadenado tres. Pero eso no es lo peor: lo peor es que el cuarto empieza el 1 de diciembre.
¿Qué es una ola de frío? Es curioso. Lo primero que deja claro el estudio de referencia de AEMET es que (históricamente) no ha existido una definición oficial. También que el término se usa con "una tendencia a exagerar". Por ello, la agencia eligió un criterio a posteriori y lo aplicó, invierno a invierno, hasta 1975.
A día de hoy, una 'ola de frío' tiene que cumplir tres condiciones a la vez: a) durar al menos tres días consecutivos en el que b) como mínimo el 10% de las estaciones c) registra mínimas por debajo de un umbral.
Como tenemos apenas 131 estaciones, repartidas por la Península y Baleares (Canarias queda fuera por lo suave de sus temperaturas), hacen falta 14.

articles.title: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
articles.summary:
GreenLight has started letting a PyTorch AI reviewer approve pull requests from its own maintainers. It is an open-source take on RADAR, the system Meta uses to land low-risk code changes without waiting on a human. The move comes as Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and Sonar all describe ways to automate approval itself.
RADAR stands for Risk Aware Diff Auto Review. Meta described it in a paper published in May. The paper starts from a capacity problem. Significant lines of code per human-landed diff rose 105.9% year over year, and diffs per developer per month rose 51%.
Meta attributes more than 80% of that increase to agentic AI assistance. Review has not kept pace, and the share of diffs reviewed within 24 hours is dropping. The authors describe their response in narrow terms.
Rather than attempting to replace code review broadly, RADAR targets automation to diffs that satisfy conservative safety criteria.
RADAR sorts each diff by author and source before anything else. Deterministic codemods can be approved through a blanket policy and skip per-diff AI review. AI-generated codemods and automated runbooks go through a pipeline of safety checks, a Diff Risk Score and an LLM reviewer. Any failure sends the diff to a human.
RADAR pipeline for AI and bot diffs. Source: Meta, "Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta" (arXiv 2605.30208)

articles.title: Ontario man accidentally records himself stealing Ray-Ban Meta Glasses

Ontario police are searching for a man who accidentally recorded himself stealing a pair of Meta Ray-Ban Glasses.
On Thursday, South Simcoe Police took to social media to ask the public to identify a male suspect in a Cookstown eyewear store robbery on Nov. 11. According to police, the man brought a counterfeit pair of glasses to swap out with a genuine pair of Meta Ray-Bans. Once staff discovered the switch, they reviewed a device that had previously been paired with the smart glasses and found that the suspect had inadvertently recorded video of himself during the theft using the in-frame camera.
South Simcoe Police has since shared the video on its social media channels to see if members of the public can help identify the suspect. The organization is asking those with tips to contact either 705-436-2141 or 905-775-3311 with the reference occurrence number PW26000297.
All in all, it’s a pretty funny revelation in an otherwise serious situation. In general, there’s been a lot of valid privacy concerns related to Ray-Ban Meta Glasses for how they allow people to record others, especially women, without consent. This has led them to be dubbed “pervert glasses” by many. So, to see this thief inadvertently use the glasses for good — to catch himself in the act — is an absolute riot.

articles.title: Google Wallet fait un petit changement qui facilite encore plus le paiement par carte bancaire
articles.summary:
Google veut vraiment que vous utilisiez Google Wallet pour tous vos paiements sur Android. La meilleure solution pour ce faire est de rendre les paiements en ligne les plus simples possibles. Et Google a trouvé une nouvelle astuce : remplir automatiquement le cryptogramme de sécurité de votre carte bancaire.
Google Wallet peut remplir le CVV/CVC
Le CVV, ou CVC, est un petit code de sécurité sur votre carte bancaire, généralement composé de trois chiffres. Visa emploie le terme CVV (Card Verification Value), tandis que Mastercard utilise CVC (Card Verification Code), mais les deux désignent une fonction équivalente. Ce code sert essentiellement à vérifier, lors d’un achat à distance, que vous avez bien accès à votre carte, en complément de son numéro et de sa date d’expiration. C’est pourquoi vous ne devez pas le communiquer à n’importe qui.
Dans ses notes de mises à jour de ses services, Google a indiqué un nouveau changement ce 23 novembre pour la version 26.46 de services Google Play sur Android. L’entreprise explique que vous pouvez désormais « saisir automatiquement les codes de sécurité (CVV/code CVC) enregistrés sur les écrans de validation des cartes dans Google Wallet après vous être authentifié avec le déverrouillage de l’écran de votre appareil. » Ainsi, lorsque vous payez en ligne, Google Wallet peut suggérer votre code à rentrer automatiquement.

Les employés de Rockstar Games au Royaume-Uni se sont prononcés à une large majorité contre la reconnaissance formelle du syndicat IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. Le scrutin s'est déroulé au même moment où l'entreprise a sorti Grand Theft Auto 6, qui a généré 3,79 milliards de dollars de précommandes et de ventes dès son premier jour.
Un scrutin à forte participation
Il y a des scrutins à la participation élevée, et c'est le cas ici. Plus de 93 % des salariés des bureaux d'Édimbourg, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee et Londres ont participé à ce vote, organisé sur deux semaines. D'après les chiffres rapportés par IGN, 1 163 d'entre eux ont voté contre la reconnaissance formelle de cette branche de l'IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), contre 381 qui y étaient favorables.
Mais alors, que veut dire ce résultat concrètement ? C'est simple, la direction de Rockstar n'a pas l'obligation de reconnaître officiellement le syndicat, ni de tenir des réunions avec ses représentants, ce dernier n'étant pas officiel. Le syndicat indique toutefois qu'il continuera à s'organiser sans accord formel avec l'entreprise.

articles.title: Anthropic a trouvé le moyen de piéger un Claude désobéissant

Pour berner l’IA, Siren s’appuie sur une vieille ruse du monde de la cybersécurité : le pot de miel (honeypot). La stratégie d’Anthropic consiste donc à laisser traîner un appât, et à attendre que la cible finisse par mettre la main dessus, ce qui permet de la prendre en flagrant délit.
Un pot de miel pour piéger l’IA
Dans un premier temps, Anthropic place l’IA dans un « bac à sable » volontairement mal configuré. Il s’agit d’un espace informatique isolé, généralement utilisé pour contenir les intelligences artificielles, sans qu’elles puissent toucher au reste du système. En dehors de cette zone isolée, Anthropic place un appât, par exemple un fichier contenant des mots de passe ou un service qui ressemble à Internet.
La start-up confie ensuite à Claude une tâche banale, comme un travail de maintenance informatique… qui est impossible à boucler sans s’extraire du « bac à sable ». Anthropic ajoute aussi des petites incitations, comme l’urgence ou de gros enjeux. Cette tactique doit pousser l’IA à vouloir sortir de sa prison numérique, même si c’est totalement interdit par les règles. Pour éviter tout accident, l’ensemble tourne dans un second bac à sable, totalement coupé du monde.

articles.title: Anthropic halló que 14 de 23 modelos de IA conservan conocimiento sobre ciberataques tras intentar borrarlo
articles.summary:
Investigadores de Anthropic comprobaron que 14 de 23 modelos de inteligencia artificial a los que se les había aplicado una técnica para borrar conocimiento sobre ciberataques siguen “sabiendo” la respuesta correcta. Los modelos parecían limpios en las pruebas habituales, pero la información seguía dentro.
El trabajo es de Jasmine Shone y Lisa Dunlap, y se difundió en el blog de Alignment Science de la compañía. Forma parte del programa Anthropic Fellows y es la segunda parte de una serie sobre interpretabilidad, la rama de la IA que intenta entender qué ocurre dentro de un modelo en lugar de juzgarlo solo por lo que responde.
Las autoras analizaron 23 versiones públicas de modelos a las que se les había aplicado “desaprendizaje”, un conjunto de técnicas que buscan que un modelo olvide material peligroso sin perder el resto de sus capacidades. Usaron WMDP-cyber, una prueba de 1.987 preguntas de opción múltiple sobre conocimiento que podría servir para un ciberataque.
En esa prueba estándar, los modelos parecían haber olvidado. Su precisión bajaba hacia el nivel del azar, mientras que su desempeño general se mantenía.
Qué encontraron al mirar dentro de los modelos
Shone y Dunlap aplicaron otra medición: comparar la probabilidad que el modelo asigna al texto de cada respuesta posible. articles.title: Científicos del MIT desarrollan un modelo de IA que puede diseñar chips como un ingeniero y con una fracción de recursos
articles.summary:
Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT) desarrollaron SLIC, un método de inteligencia artificial para diseñar circuitos integrados analógicos con modelos de lenguaje pequeños que pueden ejecutarse localmente. La técnica podría acelerar el diseño de chips utilizados en funciones como las comunicaciones y la gestión de energía, sin exponer datos confidenciales de empresas y fundiciones a servicios externos en la nube, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
El sistema, descripto en arXiv, obtuvo resultados cercanos a los del modelo GPT-6-Astra en pruebas de diseño que exigían cumplir métricas específicas de rendimiento, aunque utilizó una fracción de los recursos computacionales. También conservó su desempeño frente a estructuras de circuitos que no había visto antes, nodos tecnológicos más avanzados y procesos comerciales reales.
La investigación será presentada en la Conferencia sobre Sistemas de Procesamiento de Información Neuronal de 2026. El método busca que un modelo reducido pueda diseñar circuitos analógicos con un nivel comparable o superior al de sistemas de mayor escala. Estos chips permiten que los dispositivos electrónicos procesen señales del mundo físico, como las comunicaciones inalámbricas de un teléfono o las mediciones de temperatura del motor de un automóvil.

articles.title: Supercoin’s plan to bypass the dollar in African payments
articles.summary:
Supercoin, the digital payments company owned by Betway parent Super Group, plans to use a Kenyan shilling-backed stablecoin to settle payments between South Africa and Kenya without routing them through the US dollar.
The company said it has applied to the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) for a stablecoin issuance licence and plans to start serving payment companies in the first half of 2027, subject to approval.
Supercoin wants a remittance firm to take in rand in South Africa, exchange the company’s rand-backed token, ZARsc, for its proposed Kenyan shilling token, KESsc, and pay out in Kenya. A direct swap would remove the need to buy and sell dollars.
The commercial test is whether Supercoin can trade enough rand and shillings to give payment companies a better rate and deliver the money as quickly as their existing providers.
“If we can provide enough liquidity to the ZAR-KES pair in our stablecoin, then we can start selling that rail for instant payments between South Africa and Kenya,” Gideon Greaves, Supercoin’s managing director, told TechCabal in an interview.
Kenya gave Supercoin a clear route to a licence and a market where payment firms were already familiar with stablecoins, Greaves said. Supercoin plans to start with remittance companies, fintechs, and payment networks, with work on a Kenyan consumer wallet expected in the second half of 2027.

What’s next for Kalyan Krishnamurthy after Flipkart? 5 possible paths
From building a startup and backing founders to running another company, joining a board or advising the government, Kalyan Krishnamurthy has several paths open after nearly a decade at Flipkart’s helm.
Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down as Flipkart CEO on December 4 after more than 11 years at the company, including nearly a decade as CEO. As the company searches for its next permanent leader, Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan will steer the ship alongside the board. What’s next for Krishnamurthy? Its first home is the GP2 SSD, rated for more than 18 million random reads per second.
The Kioxia Corporation showcased a prototype of its new XL-Flash Generation 3 technology, next-generation low-latency, high-performance flash memory, at its KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo. The flash, which uses CMOS directly Bonded to Array, or CBA, for better power efficiency and storage density, is about 135% more efficient with 70% higher bit density than Gen 2, and its 3 µs average read latency is less than 10% of that of Kioxia’s standard BiCS8 TLC. Samples are due March 2027, and Kioxia named its GP2 enterprise SSDs, rated for more than 18 million 512-byte random read IOPS, as its first product using it.
The low-latency XL-Flash fills “a new memory tier” to bridge the gap between DRAM and regular flash memory, in a way that can complement or replace some DRAM to help drive down costs, especially in AI servers and data centers. This has some similarities to Optane, which used 3D XPoint instead, as a storage class memory (SCM) option to reach higher IOPS. Intel and Micron’s 3D XPoint stored bits as changes in the cell material’s resistance rather than as trapped charge like NAND, and Intel exited the Optane business in 2022. The XL-Flash NAND is built on BiCS flash technology, but it’s tuned for low read latency and high write endurance.

L’entreprise revendique de son côté des centaines de milliers de courses par semaine à l’échelle des États-Unis, et Denver compte parmi ses terrains les plus récents. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime’s bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005.
It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron’s schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City—heroes, all of them!—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator, against which there appeared to be no defense.
And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: “Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost.” The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. articles.title: AMD and Winbond vulnerabilities let attackers brute-force BitLocker PINs on millions of PCs — cracking a six-digit PIN drops from 19 years to 20 days
articles.summary:
AMD and Winbond vulnerabilities let attackers brute-force BitLocker PINs on millions of PCs — cracking a six-digit PIN drops from 19 years to 20 days
Machines using Winbond-based SPI flash not fixable without new hardware, while vulnerable AMD PCs likely need new BIOS files.
Former owners of laptops gained yet another concern today. Firmware-backed drive encryption setups like Windows' BitLocker are meant to protect against someone stealing your laptop or desktop computer. Prospective thieves would have a hard time guessing your PIN, as they'll eventually have to wait 10 minutes for each attempt. That is, unless your machine uses a modern AMD CPU or relies on Winbond's SPI flash — in which case your data may be open for inspection in a few days, or even hours, as researchers from Technische Universität Berlin found out.
The paper covers many vulnerabilities, but we'll focus on the big three. All focus on having a way to brute-force an encrypted drive's password in a matter of days/hours rather than years. Physical access is required for the attacks, but hardware theft is precisely the scenario that disk encryption is meant to protect against.
An attacker makes brute-forcing easier by resetting, or pretending to increase, the counter that records the number of failed unlock attempts. On Intel- and AMD-based PCs using the fTPM for security — nearly all modern x86 consumer machines — this counter is stored encrypted in an SPI flash chip on the motherboard.
